observations.body: David contrasts his cedar house with the ark’s tent; Nathan first agrees, then delivers a word recounting God’s movement, David’s rise, Israel’s rest, a promised house, offspring, throne, discipline, and enduring love.

payload.posture: Read 2 Samuel 7:1–17 as its own ark, house, and kingdom David setting before carrying its language into another source.
payload.tension: The source places David’s building desire is answered by a promise that God will build David a house inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
